Given that the polar equation of the circle is $r=6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta <\frac{\pi }{2},$ construct an integral that represents the area of this circle in polar coordinates.

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                         $\,\,\text{d}\theta $
feedback.worked_solution:
In general, the area of the region bounded by a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ and the rays $\theta ={\theta }_{1}$ and $\theta ={\theta }_{2}$ is given by the formula

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Therefore, the area of our circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}36{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}18{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
